transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… yeah, hi. I guess the main thing is my eating’s gotten really off lately. Like, some days before work I only manage coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I’m running around in my scrubs all shift—well, not running exactly, but you know how it is in healthcare support, there’s always something—and I realized my scrubs are kind of hanging loose on me now.

I’m not trying to lose weight or anything. It just sort of… happened.
When you eat less, is it mostly because you just don’t feel hungry?

Yeah, I think… mostly, yeah. It’s like I don’t really feel hungry, or I don’t notice it until later. I’ll have coffee and maybe a granola bar before work, and then once I’m in my scrubs and the shift starts, I just kind of keep going.

And then I get home and realize, oh, I didn’t really eat. My scrubs are loose now, which is weird because I’m not trying to lose weight or anything. It just kind of slipped away from me.
Are you avoiding food because you’re worried about gaining weight?

No, not like… I’m not avoiding it because I’m worried I’ll gain weight. It’s more that food just kind of falls off the list. I’ll have coffee and maybe a granola bar before my shift, and then once I’m at work in my scrubs, moving around, answering people, doing the usual stuff, I don’t really stop.

Then I notice later my scrubs are hanging loose, which bothers me because I’m not trying to lose weight. It just sort of happened.
Did this start after something stressful happened in your life?

Yeah… I guess it kind of did. Not like one big dramatic thing, but when the clinic changed the EMR and redid all the workflow stuff, my hours shifted around and everything got more… I don’t know, chopped up.

That’s when it started, I think. It’s been going on since then—almost two years now, which sounds longer when I say it out loud. The whole schedule got weird, and then eating just sort of stopped being a normal part of the day.
Do you feel anxious most days?

I don’t know… anxious most days? I’m not sure I’d call it that. Some days I feel keyed up, I guess, but then other days I’m just trying to get through the shift and the little stuff, like whether I packed something or where I put my badge.

I mean, work can make anybody tense, right? Especially when people are waiting on you and the computer’s doing whatever it wants. But “most days”… I’d have to think about that. I haven’t really been tracking it that way.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess I have. I used to run over in Van Cortlandt Park, not like serious marathon stuff, just enough to clear my head. And I’d take photos sometimes, little things, the trees or people playing baseball, whatever caught my eye.

I used to play chess with friends too, but lately when I think about doing any of that, I just kind of tell myself, “What’s the point?” Then I end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or checking my budget spreadsheet again, which is not exactly a hobby.
Have you been feeling down or depressed?

Yeah… I mean, yeah. Mornings are the worst, I think. I wake up and it’s like this heavy, hollow feeling is already sitting there, like the day’s ruined before I even get up, before I even put on my badge.

And then I’m thinking about stupid stuff too, like whether the badge reel is in my jacket or if I left it by the sink, because I did that once and had to go all the way back—sorry, that’s not really what you asked. But yeah, down. That’s probably the word.
Have you had thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

I… yeah, sometimes. Not like I’ve made a plan or anything like that. I haven’t sat down and thought, “I’m going to do this.” It’s more like… I’ll wake up and think it would’ve been easier if I just didn’t wake up at all.

Or I catch myself thinking maybe if I disappeared, people wouldn’t have to deal with me. Then I’ll start thinking about bills or whether I left something at work, and I kind of shove it aside. But yeah… those thoughts come up.
How has your sleep been lately?

Not great. I’ll get into bed and I’m tired, but then I’m just lying there replaying stuff from work, like what I should’ve done differently or whether I forgot something. And I start listening for noises too, like every little sound in the hallway or outside, which is ridiculous, but I still do it.

Then I’ll finally sleep some, but I keep waking up around 3 or 4 in the morning. After that I can’t really settle back down before the alarm goes off, so I’m just kind of waiting for the day to start.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah… I do. It’s not always like I can’t read or anything, but I lose the thread really fast.

Like at work, someone will ask me a simple intake question, just one thing, and I’ll start answering but then I’m explaining what screen it is in the EMR, and then I’m talking about how short we were staffed that day, and then somehow I’m bringing up something I read for licensure… and I can see on their face that I’m not answering what they asked anymore.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. I know there was a point, but I kind of drift away from it.
Have you been feeling guilty or like you’re a burden to other people?

Yeah… I do. I keep feeling like I’m just making things harder for everybody. Like at the clinic, if I’m a little slow turning over a room or I miss some small thing, I’ll go home thinking I ruined the whole flow of the day for everyone.

And with my family too… I start thinking they’d be better off if they didn’t have to worry about me. It sounds dramatic when I say it, because it might just be one little delay or one mistake, but in my head it turns into this big thing, like I’ve burdened everybody.
For at least two weeks, have you felt down like this nearly every day?

Yeah… I mean, it’s been pretty much every day. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge.

And then I’ll start thinking about getting to work, the parking, who’s on the schedule, whether I’m going to mess something up… but the feeling is already there before any of that. It’s just there when I wake up.
Have you been moving or talking noticeably slower than usual?

Yeah… I think so. It’s kind of one or the other.

At work I’ll catch myself pacing around the supply area, opening the same drawers over and over like I’m checking for something, even though I already looked. And then other times I’m just… slow. Like drawing up labels, answering a patient, stuff that should be quick, it takes me twice as long.

And then I start thinking about how the drawers are never stocked the same way depending on who closed the night before, which probably isn’t even the point… but yeah, people can probably notice I’m either restless or moving really slowly.
Have you lost weight recently?

Yeah… I think I have. I haven’t been trying to or anything, but my scrubs are hanging looser than they used to.

It’s more like my eating’s been all messed up. Some days before a shift I’ll just have coffee and maybe a granola bar, and then I realize later I never really ate. The break room has stuff sometimes, but then I get thinking about whether it’s someone’s food or if I’m taking too long on break… anyway, yeah, I’ve noticed my clothes fitting looser.
When your scrubs feel looser, do you feel good about that?

Not really, no. It’s not like I’m proud of it or trying to fit into something smaller.

It’s more… I notice my scrubs hanging off me and it kind of worries me, because I know I’m not eating right. Some mornings it’s just coffee and maybe a granola bar before a shift, and then the whole day gets away from me. And with scrubs, you know, they’re already kind of loose, depending on the brand and the hospital laundry and all that, but this is different. I’m not trying to lose weight.
Have you had much less appetite lately?

Yeah… a lot less, I think. What brings me in is more that my eating has gotten so off, like some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and then suddenly it’s hours later.

It’s weird because in the break room there’s food sometimes, but then I get caught up thinking whose it is, or whether I’m taking too long, or if I should’ve packed something better… and then I just don’t eat. So yeah, my appetite’s definitely been low, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
When your eating drops off, is it mainly because you feel depressed?

Yeah… I mean, I think that’s a big part of it. It’s not like I’m just busy and forget every time.

Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even put on my badge. And then breakfast just feels… pointless, or too much effort. I’ll stand there looking at the kitchen like I should do something, but then I start thinking about being late, or how the parking garage is going to be, and then I just grab coffee and leave.
Before this started, was there ever a stretch of at least two months when you felt mostly okay emotionally?

Before it really settled in? Yeah, I think there was… I mean, I wasn’t walking around thrilled or anything, but there were times I was mostly okay emotionally.

The steady low mood and not really caring about things, that came later. It’s been going on now for, I guess, about a year and four months. I always try to line it up with work schedules, because that’s how I remember time—like which unit I was floated to, who was on nights—but yeah, roughly sixteen months where it’s been pretty constant.

doctor.intent: Differentiate a primary depressive episode from an eating disorder or nonspecific stress/anxiety by checking for abnormally low appetite as a neurovegetative symptom of depression.
doctor.question: Have you had much less appetite lately?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: What brings me in is that my eating has gotten so off that some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly asking about decreased appetite lately, which matches the appetite/weight change symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah… a lot less, I think. What brings me in is more that my eating has gotten so off, like some days I barely get down coffee and a granola bar before a shift, and then suddenly it’s hours later.

It’s weird because in the break room there’s food sometimes, but then I get caught up thinking whose it is, or whether I’m taking too long, or if I should’ve packed something better… and then I just don’t eat. So yeah, my appetite’s definitely been low, and my scrubs have been hanging loose even though I’m not trying to lose weight.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the reduced eating is driven by low mood rather than a primary eating disorder, to distinguish major depressive disorder from OSFED/unspecified feeding or eating disorder.
doctor.question: When your eating drops off, is it mainly because you feel depressed?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling like the day is already ruined before I even put on my badge.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the reduced eating is mainly connected to feeling depressed, so the most direct symptom to use is depressed mood.

patient.answer:
Yeah… I mean, I think that’s a big part of it. It’s not like I’m just busy and forget every time.

Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day’s already ruined before I even put on my badge. And then breakfast just feels… pointless, or too much effort. I’ll stand there looking at the kitchen like I should do something, but then I start thinking about being late, or how the parking garage is going to be, and then I just grab coffee and leave.

doctor.intent: Assess whether the depressive symptoms are episodic versus chronic/persistent, to distinguish major depressive episode from other stress-related or unspecified conditions.
doctor.question: Before this started, was there ever a stretch of at least two months when you felt mostly okay emotionally?

target_item.name: Depressive Episode Duration
target_item.manifestation: The steady depression and loss of interest settled in later, and it has been with me for roughly the past year and four months.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timing and duration of emotional/depressive symptoms, specifically whether there was a sustained period of feeling emotionally okay before the current depressive stretch began.

patient.answer:
Before it really settled in? Yeah, I think there was… I mean, I wasn’t walking around thrilled or anything, but there were times I was mostly okay emotionally.

The steady low mood and not really caring about things, that came later. It’s been going on now for, I guess, about a year and four months. I always try to line it up with work schedules, because that’s how I remember time—like which unit I was floated to, who was on nights—but yeah, roughly sixteen months where it’s been pretty constant.

inference.note: History now supports recurrent depressive disorder rather than a single current episode: there was a prior period of at least 2 months feeling mostly okay before the current ~16-month depressive syndrome, with neurovegetative symptoms, anhedonia, guilt, poor concentration, psychomotor change, weight loss/decreased appetite, insomnia, and passive death wishes. F32.A is replaced by F33.1. Eating disturbance appears secondary to depression rather than weight/shape concerns, so feeding/eating disorder NOS remains only as a differential.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a persistent depressive syndrome lasting about 16 months with depressed mood nearly every day, markedly diminished interest, insomnia with early morning awakening, low appetite with unintentional weight loss, impaired concentration, guilt/worthlessness, psychomotor change, and passive death wishes. Symptoms meet criteria for a major depressive episode and are not better explained by body-image-driven eating pathology; reduced intake appears secondary to depression. History of prior periods of feeling mostly okay for at least two months supports recurrent rather than chronic uninterrupted depressive symptoms. Severity is consistent with moderate recurrent depressive disorder.
